Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of items before we can put the pilot on the 20–week schedule:

- Mediplex needs confirmation that Redwood can accept a temporary carve-out for logs/telemetry being processed by CloudBridge (a log processor) which routes logs through the US for enrichment. This will only affect diagnostic logs for the 90-day pilot.
- We need the latest DPA redline and evidence pack (SOC2, encryption, subprocessor list) to pass our legal review.
- Procurement has a signed deadline of 2026-01-20 for DocuSign return for the pilot MSA addendum.

If Redwood is open to a narrowly scoped cross-border exception plus the mitigations below, we can proceed:
- Strict TTL (30d) on logs, pseudonymization where possible, and documented access controls for CloudBridge.
- A delegation letter from CloudBridge describing processing locations and security controls.

Can you confirm feasibility and share the DPA/Docusign link? If useful, loop in legal/security.

Thanks,

Thanks — technical note from infra side. CloudBridge will be used only for log enrichment and routing; they have a US processing leg (us-east) for enrichment jobs. Concrete mitigations we can offer for the pilot:

- Encrypt logs at rest and in transit. We will provision envelope keys scoped to the pilot; root key can remain in EU KMS if Mediplex requires (option: customer-managed key for EU-only custody as paid add-on).
- TTL: automatic purge of diagnostic logs after 30 days.
- Pseudonymization: redact user identifiers where possible before shipping to CloudBridge.
- Access: role-based access only for CloudBridge, limited to support/service accounts; no human access without escalation.
- Audit trail: we will include an access and egress log slice in the evidence pack.

Attached: CloudBridge_subprocessor_delegation_statement.pdf (delegation statement received from CloudBridge). Please confirm which log buckets are in-scope so we can enforce redaction rules.

—Kimberly Park | Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

A few security asks to add to the DPA/TIA for pilot scoping:

- Define a TIA (temporary impact assessment) appendix that enumerates allowed telemetry fields and specifically prohibits shipping PII.
- Implement a short-lived fallback: if CloudBridge is unavailable we will route logs to EU-only queue and pause enrichment jobs.
- Tokenization: where Mediplex requires identifiers for debugging, use one-way tokenization before sending to CloudBridge.
- Incident notification SLA: 48-hour initial notice and 7-day remediation update.

Attached: SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf (evidence). I confirm SOC2 is current and the controls referenced map to the delegation statement.

If Mediplex accepts these TIA items, we can finalize the DPA with a UK IDTA mapping for the pilot only.
